title: Zirconia veneers vs e.max veneers: the real truth
seoTitle: Zirconia vs e.max Veneers: Strength, Thickness, Lifespan
description: Zirconia is two to three times stronger, keeps more tooth under a crown and holds its edge at the gum line. Where e.max is still the honest choice.
author: Dr. Gretell Alonso Fiel, DMD
imageAlt: A layered zirconia veneer and a single-shade glass ceramic veneer side by side on linen, lit from behind
answer: Both are porcelain, but not the same porcelain. **Zirconia** is two to three times stronger than lithium disilicate, sold as **e.max**: it keeps more tooth under a crown, survives heavy bites and bridges, and can finish its edge at the gum line instead of under it. e.max is a good glass ceramic for a single front tooth. Every piece we make is zirconia, hand-finished in the building.

blocks.p: When a clinic says porcelain veneers, it means a dental ceramic, and there are two families in common use. **Lithium disilicate** is a glass ceramic; the best-known brand is IPS e.max, and in many clinics 'e.max' has become the word for the material. **Zirconia**, zirconium dioxide, is a crystalline ceramic that started life in crowns and bridges because of its strength and now comes in multilayer discs translucent enough for front teeth.

So the question is not porcelain versus something else. It is which porcelain, and the difference shows up in four places: how strong it is, how much tooth it costs you, where its edge can sit, and how the color is built. Those four decide how your smile looks and holds up at year ten, not at delivery.
We use zirconia for every veneer, crown and bridge we make. This article explains why, and is honest about where e.max remains a perfectly good choice.

sections.h2: Strength: the number that decides where you can use it

blocks.p: Strength in ceramics is measured as flexural strength, in megapascals. Ivoclar's own figure for IPS e.max is [about 470 MPa](https://zoolu.ivoclar.com/zoolu-website/media/document/1256/IPS+e-max+Press+-+Lab+to+Dentist). Standard 3Y zirconia is rated at roughly 1,000 to 1,200 MPa, two to three times higher. That gap is why zirconia is the default for molars, bridges and patients who grind, and why e.max is usually limited to single front teeth.

The clinical data points the same way. A 2026 meta-analysis of multi-unit bridges found five-year survival of [87.9 to 92.9% for zirconia against 82.5% for lithium disilicate](https://dental.org.il/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ijp_39_4_romandini_p_9666_p444.pdf), with ceramic chipping least frequent in monolithic zirconia. For a full set of 20 veneers, or a makeover that mixes veneers and crowns across the bite, that margin of safety is the whole point.
Strength also buys thinness. A material that bends less can be made thinner without cracking, which is where the next section starts.

sections.h2: How much tooth each one costs you

blocks.p: For veneers the two are closer than the marketing suggests. Ivoclar publishes a [0.3 mm minimum for e.max veneers](https://zoolu.ivoclar.com/zoolu-website/media/document/1256/IPS+e-max+Press+-+Lab+to+Dentist), though most labs ask for 0.5 to 0.7 mm to be safe. Our zirconia veneers are 0.3 mm, and on small or inward-set teeth sometimes nothing is removed at all. Either way, a well-made veneer in either material should stay in enamel, which is where [veneers last longest](/blog/do-veneers-ruin-your-teeth).

For crowns the difference is real. An e.max crown needs [1.0 mm walls with adhesive cementation](https://zoolu.ivoclar.com/zoolu-website/media/document/1256/IPS+e-max+Press+-+Lab+to+Dentist). A zirconia crown can be made with 0.5 mm walls. On a tooth that needs a crown, that is half a millimetre of your own tooth kept all the way round, and a preparation that stays further from the nerve.

blocks.alt: A multilayer zirconia disc on its edge showing five bands from warm ivory to translucent white, next to a single-shade lithium disilicate ingot and a thin translucent wafer

sections.h2: The edge: at the gum line, or buried under it

blocks.p: Every veneer and crown has an edge, the margin, where ceramic meets tooth. Where that edge sits matters more than most patients are told. Margins placed under the gum are associated with [more inflammation, loss of attachment and bone loss](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3284004) than margins at or above the gum line, because they crowd the fibers that attach your gum to the tooth.

Dentists bury margins for one main reason: to hide them. With a glass ceramic the bonded edge and its cement line can show or pick up stain over the years, so the fix is to tuck it out of sight. Zirconia does not discolor, so we can finish the edge exactly at the gum line, where it is visible, cleanable and easy to keep sealed, and leave the gum and bone underneath alone. That is the quiet reason zirconia smiles tend to keep their gum line.

blocks.alt: Close-up of a front tooth restored with a zirconia crown whose edge meets healthy pink gum with no dark line

sections.h2: Shade: built into the material, or added by hand

blocks.p: A natural tooth is warmer near the gum and translucent at the biting edge. Multilayer zirconia discs come with that gradient already inside: five layers of shade, warmer at the bottom, more translucent at the top. The ceramist cuts the veneer out of the right part of the disc and adds surface texture and enamel effects by hand on top of a gradient that is already there.

e.max is a single-shade block. To get a translucent edge, the ceramist cuts the veneer back and layers a separate translucent porcelain on top. It can look superb in skilled hands, but it is one more step and one more interface between materials, and that interface is where chips start. It is also why so many e.max sets are made in one flat shade: layering costs time. The result is the look we describe in [why some veneers look fake](/blog/why-veneers-look-fake).

sections.h2: Where e.max is still the honest choice

blocks.p: We would be doing what we criticise if we pretended zirconia wins every case. e.max is a fine material for a single veneer on a front tooth with a healthy bite, especially when the tooth underneath is already bright and the goal is a small change of shape. Its glass structure gives a depth of translucency that is hard to beat on one tooth next to natural neighbours, and bonded to enamel it lasts well: pooled studies put veneer survival in the mid-nineties at ten years regardless of brand.

Where it stops being the honest choice is under load: long bridges, molars, grinders, and full sets where every tooth has to match and the bite is being rebuilt. There the strength and the margin advantages of zirconia are worth more than a fraction more translucency. That is our work, which is why our lab is set up for zirconia.

blocks.p: Strength figures are the manufacturers' biaxial flexural values; thickness minimums are their published guidance. How long any restoration lasts depends on bite, gum health and care.

sections.h2: How we finish zirconia at Xiluet Smiles

blocks.p: The material is only half of it. Milled crowns rarely fit straight off the machine, so each piece is adjusted under magnification with fine burs until it seats without pressure, then the margin is polished into a closed seal that keeps bacteria out. Our ceramist works in the same building as your doctor, which is why shade is matched in person, adjustments happen the same day, and a set of 20 veneers is delivered in the same week you arrive.

sections.h2: Questions to ask any clinic, including us

list: **Which material, exactly?** Zirconia or lithium disilicate, and whether it is layered or a single shade.
**How much tooth per tooth?** A fraction of a millimetre for a veneer; half a millimetre of wall for a zirconia crown, a millimetre for e.max.
**Where will the margin sit?** At the gum line or under it, and why.
**Who finishes it, and where?** A ceramist in the building can adjust shade and fit the same day. A lab in another country cannot.
**What is in writing?** Material, number of teeth, restoration per tooth, price and warranty.

blocks.p: If you want a second opinion on a plan you already have, send photos through the [free photo evaluation](/free-photo-evaluation). A doctor replies within 6 hours with which material and which restoration each tooth honestly needs.

faq.q: Are zirconia veneers better than e.max veneers?
faq.a: For sets, crowns, bridges and anyone who grinds, yes: two to three times the strength, less tooth removed for crowns, an edge that can stay at the gum line, and shade built into the material. For a single front veneer with a healthy bite, e.max is a fine choice too.

faq.q: Do zirconia veneers look opaque or fake?
faq.a: Old zirconia did. Modern multilayer zirconia comes with five layers of shade and a translucent edge inside the disc, and our ceramist adds texture and enamel effects by hand. What makes veneers look fake is a flat single shade, and that happens in any material.

faq.q: Can zirconia veneers really be 0.3 mm?
faq.a: Yes. Because the material is so strong, 0.3 mm is our standard veneer thickness, and on some teeth nothing is removed at all. The exact amount for each tooth is confirmed at Visit 1 after the scans.

faq.q: How long do zirconia veneers last compared with e.max?
faq.a: We design zirconia work for 20 years and warrant it for 5 in writing. e.max veneers and crowns typically last 10 to 15 years, with chipping the usual reason for replacement. Bite, gum health and night guards matter as much as the material.
